questions.q: What does the hadith mention about Bilal in Paradise?
options: The sound of his footsteps heard in Paradise
questions.explain: Bilal held firm with a single word, Ahad.

questions.q: What was Zinnirah's answer to Abu Jahal, who said Allat and Uzza had blinded her?
options: Allat and Uzza bring no benefit
questions.explain: She was beaten until blind and later restored.

questions.q: How did the Prophet SAW welcome someone who gave up his wealth to migrate?
questions.explain: Wealth left behind for faith is a profitable trade.

questions.q: What was permitted to Ammar according to An-Nahl 16:106?
options: To repeat what he was forced to say while his heart stayed firm
questions.explain: An-Nahl 106 came down in defence of Ammar.

options: Hoping for victory to come quickly
questions.explain: The Prophet's admonition to Khabbab. Victory cannot be hunted.

questions.q: Allah confirmed Abu Bakr's sincerity even though he was accused of a hidden agenda.
questions.explain: True. Surah Al-Layl speaks of the one who gives wealth to purify himself.

questions.q: All strugglers see for themselves the victory they strove for.
questions.explain: False. Many died without seeing victory.

questions.q: Put these events in the right order.

items.text: Bilal is tortured and freed by Abu Bakr

questions.explain: Bilal was freed, Zinnirah beaten, Sumayyah and Yasir martyred, then An-Nahl 106 came down.

questions.q: Match each term with its meaning.

right.text: The disease of loving the world and fearing death
A unit of weight of silver
A status neither slave nor free, under a notable's protection

questions.explain: Ahad is the One, uqiyah is a weight of silver, wahn is love of the world and fear of death, and mawla is a status under protection.

questions.q: Today's blessings are the fruit of unknown struggles. What is the right attitude?
options: Appreciate those who struggled and learn the history
